use Ghul.Pipes
use Raster.IMAGE

luminance(red: ubyte, green: ubyte, blue: ubyte) -> ubyte =>
    cast ubyte(
        0.2126D * cast double(red) +
        0.7152D * cast double(green) +
        0.0722D * cast double(blue) + 0.5D
    )

to_grey(colour: IMAGE) -> ubyte[] =>
    (0..colour.width * colour.height)
        |> map(at =>
            (let seen =
                 colour.pixel(at % colour.width, at / colour.width)

             luminance(seen.red, seen.green, seen.blue)))
        |> collect_array()

to_colour(levels: ubyte[], width: int, height: int) -> IMAGE is
    let image = IMAGE(width, height)

    for at in 0..levels.count do
        image.set_pixel(
            at % width, at / width, levels[at], levels[at], levels[at]
        )
    od

    return image
si

let width = 300
let height = 200

let colour = IMAGE(width, height)

for y in 0..height do
    for x in 0..width do
        colour.set_pixel(
            x, y,
            cast ubyte(255 * x / width),
            cast ubyte(255 * y / height),
            cast ubyte(255 - 255 * x / width)
        )
    od
od

colour.colour(255ub, 0ub, 0ub)
colour.fill([(x = 30.0D, y = 30.0D),
             (x = 110.0D, y = 30.0D),
             (x = 70.0D, y = 110.0D)])

colour.colour(0ub, 255ub, 0ub)
colour.fill([(x = 120.0D, y = 30.0D),
             (x = 200.0D, y = 30.0D),
             (x = 160.0D, y = 110.0D)])

colour.colour(0ub, 0ub, 255ub)
colour.fill([(x = 210.0D, y = 30.0D),
             (x = 290.0D, y = 30.0D),
             (x = 250.0D, y = 110.0D)])

colour.write("colour.png")

let grey = to_colour(to_grey(colour), width, height)

grey.write("grey.png")

colour.show("colour.png")
grey.show("grey.png")
